answer: Ring detection resists sybils: honest attestations spread widely, but a fake farm vouches in tight inbred loops forged from one canyon. The counting rule measures how reciprocal and self-referential a cluster's edges are and discounts dense inward rings. A quartz-hard clique that only certifies itself looks nothing like the open mesh of real peers, so it earns near-zero weight no matter how many members it forges.
